purpose: Shared interactive demo data for Assistant Chat concept comparison. It is prototype data, not product canon.

behaviorNotes.scriptedReplies: User-entered text is appended exactly as typed. The prototype then plays the next prewritten response for that thread; it does not interpret the text.
behaviorNotes.initialRendering: Each thread may render only its newest initialVisibleMessageCount messages while search indexes the complete stored message list.
behaviorNotes.timestamps: All timestamps are stored as UTC ISO strings and should render in the viewer locale.
behaviorNotes.displayText: User-facing status labels use spaces and ordinary words. Internal data keys are not display copy.

messages.body: I want the recipe planner to feel useful before someone imports a single recipe. Can we talk through the first session without jumping into implementation?

Yes. I will keep this at the product level. The first session needs to explain what the app can do, let the user add or import something quickly, and avoid presenting an empty dashboard as a failure state.
I do not want a long setup wizard. I would rather let people start and ask for details only when they matter.

That changes the flow from setup-first to progressive collection. We can keep the initial path short and defer household size, dietary preferences, and pantry details until a feature actually needs them.
What happens when they paste a recipe from a site that blocks our importer?
The conversation should explain the limitation in ordinary language, preserve the pasted source, and offer a manual review path instead of returning a generic import error.
I also want the assistant to remember that I hate cilantro, but I do not want it silently changing recipes.

That creates two separate behaviors: durable preference memory and explicit recipe edits. The assistant can warn that a recipe contains cilantro and offer substitutions, but it should not alter the saved recipe without confirmation.
Can we show the shopping list and meal plan while we are still discussing them?
Those outputs can remain represented in the conversation and open in the editor area for larger review. Opening them should not remove their original message from the thread.
I changed my mind about the name. Use Tastebook in the demo, but do not make that a permanent product decision.
I will treat Tastebook as demo content only. The conversation data can use it naturally without turning the name into product canon.
The current assistant thread is hard to read. There are cards inside cards and I can only see one or two messages.

I compared the three ways this could behave without assuming one visual treatment. The first requirement is that the human conversation remains the primary reading path at the minimum width. The second is that execution details remain truthful and inspectable without appearing at the same visual weight as every sentence. The third is that a user can recover the exact time, provider, model, task duration, tool activity, subagent work, and generated artifacts after the run is complete.

The current prototype makes those layers compete with one another. A single response can contain prose, a recommendation card, a nested tool card, a diff card, a subagent block, a metadata row, and a footer summary. All of that information may be valid, but the result is difficult to scan because the boundaries do not communicate priority. At narrow width, wrapping multiplies the height of every nested surface.

For the next pass, I will preserve the complete data and interaction contracts while treating the hierarchy itself as the design problem. This paragraph intentionally continues long enough to exercise the collapsed-message control. It also includes a search target near the end: the phrase retention window nine days should be found even while this portion is hidden. Copy must still return the complete text, and Context Lens must operate on the canonical full message rather than only the visible preview.

stages.label: Thinking
stages.summary: Compared conversation readability with execution disclosure.

messages.body: That is the issue. I still need all the details, but I need the actual conversation to be much easier to follow.
Understood. The concept will be evaluated on how quickly a person can follow the user and assistant exchange at minimum width while still being able to inspect the complete activity history.
Add a goal for finishing the onboarding plan and show the tasks, but keep it possible to pause the work.
The goal is now represented as active with a visible objective, task progress, pause, edit, stop, and evidence access. The goal and task data remain separate even if a concept presents them together.
Before you continue, ask me which import sources matter most.
I've queued four short questions for this thread. The composer stays locked until you finish, skip through, or cancel the active questionnaire.

messages.body: The usage page should help me understand where my limits went without making me read raw accounting data.

The user-facing answer needs to start with recognizable activity and then allow deeper inspection. Provider limits, model usage, task activity, and context use can share data without becoming one undifferentiated table.
I also want to know whether a number is exact, estimated, or unavailable.
Each displayed value needs a value state and provenance. An estimate should not look identical to a provider-reported exact value, and unavailable data should not be rendered as zero.
How does this connect to the chat Context Ring?
The chat entry point consumes the shared usage projection. It does not calculate a second version of usage. The detailed Context surface is owned by the parallel usage redesign.
Can the assistant tell me which conversation caused a spike?
The usage record can link activity back to a thread, turn, goal, tool run, or subagent where that identity exists. The chat concept only needs to preserve the route into the owned detail surface.
The dropdown is being redesigned elsewhere. Do not redesign it again here.
Confirmed. The concept should show the required Context Ring entry point and surrounding behavior while treating the dropdown and detailed page as an external owned component.
I want to search this thread for the first time we discussed estimated values.
Current-thread search should include stored older messages, load the matching slice, and jump to the exact result without changing Context Lens state.
Now search all threads for provider limits.
All-thread search groups matches by thread. Choosing a result from another thread switches to that thread and focuses the exact message.
Can the result show that a matched message was muted?
Yes. Human search still finds canonical history. A result may disclose that the message is muted, focused, or part of a compacted range without silently changing that state.
Keep the search interaction to one bar.
There is one search field. Its result popup offers Current Thread and All Threads, with Current Thread selected by default.
Make sure the demo has enough old messages that this is real, not a three-message trick.
This thread includes older stored content outside the initial render window so both search scopes and exact-message restoration can be exercised.
Can we walk through the handoff from an approved product document into the Planning Wizard?
The parent thread creates the planning run, shows topic progress, and opens child topic conversations without turning those children into unrelated chat systems.
I want each topic to keep its own conversation, but the parent needs to show what is happening.
Each child remains a real thread with durable history. The parent projects status, task, current activity, and result while retaining a route to the full child details.

I am going to describe the Planning Wizard handoff in one long message because this is exactly the kind of user input that must not disappear or become impossible to review. The wizard receives an approved product document, creates topic conversations, lets each topic continue independently, audits completed topics in the background, and then compiles the accepted material into Plans. The user should be able to return to the parent thread and understand which topics are complete, which are waiting, and which need an answer. The text entry area must preserve this draft continuously because a crash after writing a message this long would be unacceptable. The recovery history should retain useful revisions rather than every keystroke. The phrase blue lantern checkpoint appears only near the end so search can prove that hidden text is indexed.
I saved the complete draft, including its revision history. The composer can restore it after a simulated restart, and search can find the hidden phrase even if the message is visually collapsed.
The audit should start in the background after I move to the next topic.
That produces child activity without interrupting the current topic. The parent can show aggregate working and completion counts while full audit work remains inspectable.
What happens when an audit agent needs to ask me something?
The child reports the need to the parent. The parent owns the questionnaire in the main thread, and the child shows Waiting for parent rather than asking you directly.
I should be able to skip one question without canceling the whole questionnaire.
Skip applies to the current question only. Cancel ends that questionnaire instance. Neither action affects questionnaires queued in other threads.
After I answer, keep the questions and answers in the thread but do not let them take over forever.
The completed exchange remains inline and may collapse into a compact historical representation. Its answers and origin remain inspectable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When should background audit start?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: After the user moves to the next topic.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Should a child agent ask the user directly?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The parent owns user questions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should happen after approval?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Navigate to Orchestrator and begin the Plan Compile handoff.

messages.body: Show me the plan artifact when the topic is ready.
The plan stays represented in the conversation and opens in an editor tab for review. Opening it does not remove the conversation shortcut.
The final button must say Approve And Build.
That exact label is preserved in the Planning Wizard flow and is separate from this chat concept exercise.
Good. This thread should look like an actual conversation, not a collection of component samples.
The shared demo data contains sustained back-and-forth so the design can be judged as a conversation before individual features are inspected.

revisionHistory.text: The audit should start in the background after I move to the next topic.
The audit should start in the background after I move to the next topic, and the parent should show progress.

messages.body: I have several provider plans. I need the chat controls to make the active choice clear without turning the header into a settings page.
The visible selector row keeps Persona, Model, and Mode as separate choices. Reasoning effort is chained from Model rather than presented as a fourth peer selector.
What about the provider?
Provider is resolved through the chosen model and routing state. The message metadata records the effective provider and model that actually handled the turn.
I still need to change the worktree.
The worktree control remains adjacent to the selector row and uses the same popup family for its menu behavior.
The menus need to feel like the existing model selector.
The required popup contract includes click activation, corner-origin opening, in-place resizing, submenus, shared chrome, and single-overlay behavior.
Do not use an operating system select menu.
All concept menus use the in-application popup system. Scrollable menu contents use the Puppet Master scrollbar treatment.
Can I search the model list?
Model and Persona menus remain searchable. Mode and effort can use their bounded option sets without becoming operating-system menus.
I want the selected labels to survive a narrow width.
The underlying values remain available while each selector can yield space and truncate its visible label. The visual solution is left to the concept.
Show me what happens when the effort submenu has more choices.
The popup resizes in place instead of closing and reopening as a different menu.
Reduced motion should not leave the menu half open.
Reduced-motion mode completes the state change without the spatial animation while preserving the same final menu state.
Keep all labels readable. I do not want internal enum formatting on screen.
User-facing labels use ordinary words and spaces. Internal identifiers are never exposed as underscored prose.
Research how other assistants handle long conversations, but keep the sources tied to the claims.
I will keep a source list, separate observations from inference, and show live activity without adding a permanent message for every page visited.
Open the first source in the browser.
The browser preview opens in an editor tab. The conversation retains a shortcut and the active research status continues in place.
I want to watch what the agent is doing.
The thread shows a short current-action summary while the browser session records navigation, selections, screenshots, and source references.
Use subagents for different product groups.
Three child agents are working on coding tools, general assistants, and open-source chat platforms. The collapsed group reports aggregate progress.
Can I open one child and see everything it did?
The inline group can reveal a compact per-agent summary. Full child history and evidence can open in a dedicated detail tab without removing the inline record.
One of them is waiting for clarification. Do not let it ask me directly.
That child is marked Waiting for parent. Any user question is routed through the parent questionnaire queue.
What happens when the research finishes?
The live activity condenses into grouped historical stages. The final response and source artifact remain separate from that execution history.
Keep thought streams available, but do not leave them all open.
Completed thought segments are collapsed by default. A setting may keep the currently active permitted thought stream open until that segment completes.
Show the total time too.
The message records Worked for separately from total elapsed time when waiting or pauses make them different.

messages.body: The import suite started failing after the schema change. Can you investigate without changing unrelated files?
I will scope the run to the importer, its fixtures, and the migration that changed the record shape.
Show me what is happening while it runs.
The active summary reports the current test or file. Completed commands move into the compact activity history instead of stacking as full cards.
The first failure looks like a missing field. Is that the whole problem?
Not yet. One failure is the renamed source field, and another is a stale fixture that still uses the earlier shape.
Pause before applying a migration.
The goal is paused before mutation. Existing test output and the proposed diff remain available.
What will change?
The proposed changes update the importer mapping, repair two fixtures, and add a compatibility case. The diff summary remains separate from the goal objective and task list.
I want to edit the goal so it also checks rollback behavior.
The edit triggers impact analysis and a replan event. The new rollback task is added before work resumes.
Resume it.
The goal is running again. The active status and worked duration continue from the prior execution time rather than counting the paused interval as work.
Stop if the rollback test touches production credentials.
That stop condition is part of the goal. A credential request would block with the exact reason rather than proceeding.
The current assistant response is too long. Can I collapse it?
Long completed prose can collapse to a substantial preview. Hovering the eligible message reveals the expand or collapse control.
Copy should still copy everything.
Copy uses the canonical complete message even when the visible preview is collapsed.

activeGoal.title: Repair import tests and verify rollback
activeGoal.objective: Find the schema regression, repair bounded importer files, verify forward and rollback behavior, and stop before any credentialed production action.

messages.body: I need every chat concept to work in all eight themes, not only the theme it was designed in.
The concept workspace broadcasts the selected theme to itself and every hosted concept. The actual Puppet Master Home page is not part of that theme-switching requirement.
List the eight themes we are testing.
Friendly Dark, Friendly Light, Retro Dark, Retro Light, Basic Light, Basic Dark, Glass Dark, and Glass Light.
The motion does not need to change between themes.
The motion contract can remain the same while theme tokens change the visual presentation.
Retro often exposes spacing problems.
The visual audit treats every theme as a first-class configuration and checks text wrapping, popup bounds, scrollbars, and surface collisions.
Glass can hide contrast problems, but accessibility is not the focus of this exercise.
The prototype evaluation prioritizes readability and reduced motion. Production accessibility obligations are not being retired.
Do not use colored left borders to show selection.
That older treatment is superseded for these concepts. Selected and active states must not rely on a colored left-side border.
No emoji either.
All interface symbols are SVG. Demo prose and labels contain no emoji characters.
The index page needs to change with the theme too.
The concept comparison workspace itself transforms with the theme alongside every concept preview.
Label the model clearly.
The exact model label appears on the comparison workspace and inside every concept.
Make reduced motion a real toggle.
The workspace broadcasts reduced-motion state so every concept can be reviewed with motion enabled and reduced.
I wrote a long response yesterday and closed the app before sending it. I need to know it will come back.
Each thread has an independent durable composer draft. The latest draft restores after restart without being sent automatically.
I changed the wording several times. Can I get an earlier version?
The prototype includes a bounded, deduplicated revision history with useful recovery points rather than a new record for every keystroke.
Does switching threads overwrite it?
No. Switching threads saves the current draft and restores the other thread’s draft.
What about attachments?
Draft attachment references and relevant composer state persist with the text.
Questionnaire answers should not be mixed into that history.
Questionnaire drafts use their own thread-scoped persistence and do not appear as normal composer revisions.
Spell check needs to work in the message box.
The composer enables the platform spellcheck behavior while retaining the custom Puppet Master visual treatment.
Show me the send button while the agent is already working.
With an empty composer it is Stop. When the user starts typing, it becomes Send even while the current run continues.
What if I erase what I typed?
If the active run is still working and the draft becomes empty again, the button returns to Stop.
Sending must not accidentally stop the run.
Send and Stop are distinct actions. Submitting typed text follows the active-run steering or queue policy.
Simulate a crash and restore this draft.
The demo can reload state from local persistence and show the recovered draft and its revision history.

messages.body: I know we decided how muted messages should behave in search, but I cannot find it.
Search the canonical stored history rather than only the loaded viewport. The result can disclose the muted state without changing it.
Search only this thread first.
Current Thread is selected. Results include older messages that are not currently rendered.
The phrase was probably canonical source history.
There are several matches. The most relevant one says that Subcompact preserves canonical source history and rehydration handles.
Jump to it.
The required historical slice is loaded and the exact message receives a temporary highlight.
Now show all threads.
The same search field switches to All Threads and groups matches under their thread titles.
Do not lose my place when I return.
The current thread retains its scroll anchor, search query, scope, selected result, and Context Lens state.
Can search find text hidden by a long-message collapse?
Yes. Selecting that result expands or reveals the matching portion without changing the stored full message.
Can it find a message that is part of a compacted range?
Yes. The result resolves to the canonical source range and avoids presenting the summary and its source as unrelated duplicates.
I want enough history in this demo to prove this works.
This thread includes a large stored transcript and initially renders only its newest window.
Good. Add some repeated decisions so grouping and match counts are visible.
The stress history includes repeated terms across many dates and unique phrases that can be used as exact search targets.

Review this pull request, but keep the conversation understandable before showing every changed file.
I will summarize the intent and risks first. File-level changes remain available in the diff surface and can be expanded when needed.
There are twelve files. Do not put twelve full diffs in the transcript.
The thread can show a compact aggregate and a bounded file list while the complete diff opens in the owned editor surface.
Use subagents for tests, security, and UI behavior.
Three reviewers are working in parallel. The inline group shows their task, current activity, status, and aggregate completion.
The security reviewer found a problem.
The group now shows one blocked finding. Expanding it reveals a short reason and a route to the full review details.
Can I keep reading earlier messages while they work?
Yes. Live updates modify the existing activity and subagent records without forcing the scroll position to the bottom.
Show me the exact provider and model used for the final review.
The hover metadata row records the effective provider and model. More Info includes the timestamp and full runtime details.
The last user message can still be edited, right?
Edit appears only while the message is eligible. Earlier messages omit the control instead of showing a disabled action.
Do not show Resend.
Resend is removed. Editing and submitting the revised message replaces that workflow.
Open the combined diff.
The inline shortcut remains in the thread while the full diff opens in an editor tab.
Stop the review after the current test finishes.
The composer shows Stop while empty. The run records the terminal state and retains the work duration accumulated before stopping.
Start a goal to build the chat concept comparison workspace.
The goal is running with its objective, constraints, task list, evidence links, and child work visible from this thread.
Show the goal without expanding every task.
The collapsed goal remains discoverable and shows its state and progress. The full objective and controls are available when expanded.
Add a task for testing every theme and width.
The task list now includes the 32 theme-width configurations and records that the fake application rail is checked open and closed.
Use subagents heavily so the main agent does not carry all the context.
Bounded child assignments cover plan verification, concept modules, motion checks, demo data, automated tests, and visual audits.
I need to edit the goal. Add the fifteen-thread demo requirement.
The goal pauses scheduling, records the edit, updates impacted tasks, and then exposes the revised plan before resuming.
Resume.
The goal is running with the revised demo-data task and preserved prior evidence.
What is the agent doing now?
The current activity summary says it is checking the minimum-width message hierarchy. The worked timer updates in place.
How many subagents are still working?
Four are working, three are complete, and one is waiting for parent review.
Open the evidence.
The goal evidence route opens the detailed run surface while the thread keeps its compact goal record.
Do not let the goal controls disappear when the chat is popped out.

messages.body: The agent has two questionnaires waiting. What should I see first?
The oldest unresolved questionnaire in this thread is shown first. The newer one remains queued.
Can I keep chatting while it is open?
Not yet — finish, skip, or cancel the active questionnaire first, then the composer unlocks.
If I skip question two, does the next questionnaire open immediately?
No. Skip advances within the current questionnaire. The next queued questionnaire appears only after the current questionnaire is submitted or cancelled.
Can I go back and answer a skipped question?
Yes. A skipped question can be revisited before final submission, and answering it replaces the skipped state.
What does Cancel do?
Cancel ends the entire current questionnaire and records a cancelled result. It does not cancel the next queued questionnaire or questionnaires in other threads.
Close the app while I am halfway through.
The current page, selected answers, skipped states, and freeform draft persist. Returning to this thread shows the same questionnaire.
There should be no expiration timer.
Unresolved questionnaires do not expire passively. They remain until the user resolves them.
After I submit, keep a record here.
The questions and answers remain inline in the conversation and may collapse into a compact historical block.
Can Goal and Todo keep updating behind it?
Their state can continue updating while the questionnaire has visual priority. When the questionnaire closes, the latest state reappears.
This is enough. Leave the oldest questionnaire on question two.
The demo state is saved with question two active and the second questionnaire still queued.

messages.body: Turn this conversation into a project brief I can review next to the chat.
The generated brief is represented in this message and stored in the project so it can be reopened later.
Open it.
It opens in an editor tab. The inline artifact remains in the thread as a shortcut.
Do not mark the message as active just because the tab is open.
The artifact shortcut does not gain a required open-state treatment. The editor owns its tab state.
Can I find the file manually?
Yes. The artifact has a project path and can be opened through the file explorer.
There are three artifacts from this response. Keep them together.
The response may group related artifacts while each keeps its own title, type, path, and open action.
One of them is a browser capture.
Browser previews also open in editor tabs and retain their source relationship to the conversation.
What if I scroll this message out of view?
The editor tab remains open. Virtualizing the source message does not close or invalidate the artifact.
Search for the brief title.
Search can jump back to the source message even if it is outside the current render window.
Copy the assistant message.
Copy returns the complete message text. Artifact payloads remain separate project files.
Show the timestamp in More Info.
The message metadata includes the exact sent, start, and completed timestamps along with Worked for and total elapsed values.
The audit is blocked. I need to know exactly why, not just see a red status.
The goal reports that a test requested a credential outside the approved scope. It includes the affected task, attempted recovery, and next safe action.
Can the other subagents finish while that one is blocked?
Independent work can continue. The aggregate group shows working, complete, blocked, and waiting counts separately.
Open the blocked agent.
The inline row exposes its task and short reason. The full group details can open in a dedicated tab for complete history and evidence.
Do not show internal status names with underscores.
The visible label is Waiting for parent or Blocked, while internal identifiers remain in diagnostics only.
Pause the goal while I decide whether to approve the credential.
The goal is paused and retains its exact blocker. Worked duration stops increasing during the explicit pause.
The question should appear in this thread, not inside the child card.
The parent owns the questionnaire. The child remains in Waiting for parent until the answer is passed back.
Cancel the questionnaire instead of answering it.
Cancelling ends that questionnaire instance and returns a cancelled result to the parent. The goal remains paused until another action resolves the blocker.
Show the diff that is already complete.
The completed diff remains available even though the goal is blocked and the question was cancelled.
I want the active thought stream hidden by default.
The setting is off in this thread, so active and completed thought segments remain collapsed unless opened manually.
Stop the goal.
The goal enters Stopped rather than Clear. Its objective, evidence, task history, and worked duration remain inspectable.

messages.body: I want to build a small dashboard for my home media server this weekend, but I only have a few hours.
Start by choosing one useful view and one reliable data source. A compact first goal will be easier to finish than a broad monitoring suite.
The most useful thing would be seeing which downloads are stuck.
Then the first view can focus on active downloads, stalled duration, and a clear route to the source application.
I also want storage space, but that can wait.
I will keep storage capacity as a later task rather than expanding the first goal.
Can you give me a plan that fits Saturday afternoon?
A practical sequence is: confirm the API, render a simple list, add stalled-state rules, test with a saved response, and package a local run command.
I am not sure which framework to use.
That choice can remain open until we confirm the API and deployment target. The conversation does not need to force a framework decision yet.
Ask me what machine it will run on.
I have prepared a short question about the target machine and how you want to access the dashboard.
Actually, skip that for now. I am just checking how the chat looks.
The question can be skipped without cancelling the rest of the conversation. This thread remains ordinary and does not require a goal or subagents.
Give me a longer explanation so I can test message collapsing.

A longer project explanation can cover scope, data access, refresh behavior, failure handling, and a realistic stopping point. The important interface behavior is that the message can show a useful preview, expand on demand, preserve its scroll anchor, and still copy and search the complete content.
Now I want to type a message while your fake response is working.
The demo allows that. The button changes from Stop to Send as soon as the draft contains text.
This is a good ordinary thread for comparison.
It provides sustained back-and-forth without relying on dense internal implementation language.
